summary: Karl Friedrich Neumann worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Heidelberg, Munich, Göttingen (under Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren), San Lazzaro degli Armeni, and under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat. He served as professor at Munich (1833-1852) and curator at the Bavarian State Library (~1833-1863).
Karl G. Heider studied at Williams College (~1952-1954), Harvard College (~1954-1956), and Harvard University (~1957-1966).

Karl Georg Zistl was an Indologist who studied at the University of Munich under Ernst Kuhn (~1904-1910). He worked as a wissenschaftlicher Hilfsarbeiter at the Munich University Library from 1911 to 1952.
Karl Gottlieb Ewald Rhenius worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Berlin Mission Seminary in 1810 and served as a missionary for the Church Mission Society from around 1814 to 1835.

Karl Graul worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied theology at the University of Leipzig in 1834, directed the Leipzig Evangelical Lutheran Mission (1844-1860), and taught Missionswissenschaft at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg starting in 1861.

Karl H. Potter worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of California and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as a professor at Minnesota (~1956-1970) and Washington (~1970-1997), and edited the Encyclopedia of Indian Philosophies (~1970-2019).

Karl Hoffmann worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Munich under Ferdinand Sommer, Hanns Oertel, and Walther Wüst. He held posts at Munich, Saarland University (1952-1955), and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (1955-1983).

Karl Hummel worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at Munich under Wilhelm Geiger and at Tübingen under Enno Littmann. At the University of Tübingen, he was a botany assistant (1935) and director (1946-1976), later visiting Tehran (1975-1976).

Karl Jahn worked in Iranian/Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Charles University under Moriz Winternitz and at Leipzig. He held posts at the German University in Prague, Utrecht University (1950-1972), Leiden University (1953-1973), Istanbul, and Vienna.
Karl Jaspers was a philosopher who studied at Heidelberg University (~1902-1908). He later held an academic post at Heidelberg University from around 1913 to 1948.

Karl Jettmar specialized in history/archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna under Robert von Heine-Geldern and Robert Bleichsteiner. His posts included the Museum of Ethnology, Vienna, Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, and Heidelberg University (1964-1986).

Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Mainz and Würzburg. He served as professor at the Gymnasium and Lyceum in Aschaffenburg (1803), court librarian in Aschaffenburg (1811), and professor at the University of Bonn (1818).

Karl Lachmann worked in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1809-1812) and the University of Göttingen (~1812-1815), and he held a post at the Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1825 to 1851.

Karl Marx was a philosopher who studied at Bonn (under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker), Humboldt University of Berlin, and Jena. He held posts at the Rheinische Zeitung (~1842-1843) and the Neue Rheinische Zeitung (~1848-1849).

Karl Müllenhoff worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Meldorfer Gelehrtenschule, Kiel University, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Leipzig. He later held posts at Kiel University (1842) and Frederick William University Berlin (1858).

Karl Otfried Müller worked in history/archaeology and linguistics. He studied at Breslau and Humboldt University of Berlin under August Boeckh, Friedrich Schleiermacher, and Friedrich August Wolf. He held posts at Magdalenaeum Wrocław (1818-1819) and the University of Göttingen (1819, 1823).

Karl Popper was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vienna and the University of Cambridge. He held academic posts at the University of Canterbury (1937-1945), London School of Economics (1946), King's College London, and the University of London (1949-1969).

Karl Reinhardt worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at Bonn and Humboldt University of Berlin under Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff. He held posts at Bonn (~1912-1916), Hamburg (~1919-1924), Goethe University Frankfurt (~1924-1942), and Leipzig (~1942-1946).

Karl Richard Lepsius worked in history/archaeology and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Berlin under August Boeckh. He held posts at the German Archaeological Institute at Rome, Humboldt University of Berlin, Egyptian Museum of Berlin, and Prussian State Library.

Karl Rosenkranz was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel, as well as Heidelberg and Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1831) and the University of Königsberg (1833).
